note: Rewritten from the species-level description of Anenteotermes hemerus in Sands (1972), original in English; the species has no soldiers; measurement-table headings, figure numbers, type locality, vernacular names and biological records are not translated, and several OCR-corrupted figures in the measurement table are omitted.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The largest species of the genus. Its comparisons with A. amachetus, A. ateuchestes, A. cicur, A. cnaphorus and A. disluctans are given under those species. Of the remaining species, A. improcinctus, A. nanus and A. polyscolus are much smaller and are not easily confused with it; A. improelatans is also smaller, but the difference is less pronounced. Alates are recognizable by the weaker constriction of the meso- and metanotum and by the very small fontanelle; in workers the first and second marginal teeth of the right mandible are equal in length and the enteric mixed segment is shorter. The worker abdomen appears to be of the dehiscent type.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule yellow, pilosity orange-yellow, setae numerous but fine and inconspicuous. Postclypeus weakly inflated, Pcl/W 0.26, Pcl/Ri 1.61. Mandibular apical teeth short, La/Li 0.57, Ra/Ri 0.64; the accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible just clears the molar prominence in surface view, composite ratio 10.31; the first marginal tooth of the right mandible lies slightly behind the line from the apical tooth to the second marginal tooth, and its anterior margin is distinctly shorter than that of the second marginal tooth, composite ratio 12.07. Fore tibia slightly inflated, T1/Tw 4.50, the third apical spur about half the length of the other two. The midgut-hindgut overlap is about four times the midgut width at the attachment of the Malpighian tubules; the enteric valve seating is very weakly trilobate, connected by a short neck to the second hindgut pouch, lateral in the unopened abdomen; the enteric valve cushions are entirely retracted and of roughly equal development, with only a scaly surface; the membranous wall between the cushions bears very sparse minute spines.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule dark deep brown, darker above the ocelli; fontanelle short oval, about half the ocellus, slightly concave, brown; the median spot oval, flat, smaller than the fontanelle, concolorous with the head capsule; postclypeus dark brown, labrum yellowish brown; frontal mark a flat crescent, concolorous with the head capsule; antennae yellowish brown. Pronotum dark brown, meso- and metanotal plates yellowish brown, transverse sutures present only on the mesonotum; femora pale yellowish brown, tibiae and tarsi yellow. Abdominal tergites and the dorsal and ventral pleural spiracles brown, sternites pale brown laterally and paler medially; cerci yellow. Posterior margin of head capsule evenly rounded; ocelli medium-sized, separated from the compound eye by two-fifths to slightly more than half their own minimum diameter; postclypeus weakly inflated, Pcl/W 0.25, posterior margin arcuate, median suture present and weak at both ends. Mandibular apical teeth short, La/Li 0.54–0.56, Ra/Ri 0.66–0.69; the accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible clears the molar prominence in surface view, composite ratio 7.37–8.70; the tips of the apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible lie roughly in one line, the anterior margins of the marginal teeth about equal or the first slightly longer than the second, composite ratio 20.60–22.30. Head capsule pilosity uneven, brown, not felt-like.
